Emission figures produced with Senseible are calculated estimates based on the documents and data a customer supplies. They are self-declared by the customer. They are not certified, audited or independently verified unless a separate written verification statement says so, and Senseible does not guarantee that any regulator, lender, investor, buyer or other third party will accept them.

Emissions (E, in kilograms of CO₂-equivalent) equal the amount of activity (A: litres of fuel, kilowatt-hours, tonne-kilometres) multiplied by an emission factor (EF: kilograms of CO₂-equivalent released per unit of that activity). For example, 100 litres of a fuel with an illustrative factor of 2.5 kgCO₂e per litre gives 100 × 2.5 = 250 kgCO₂e. This is the form the IPCC and the GHG Protocol use for fuel combustion and purchased energy.
